_metadata.description: P1.6 omega/fish-oil rubric. Reviewed purpose evidence is resolved from INGR_OMEGA3 through evidence_resolver against the shared directed daily-exposure interval; the 250 mg Evidence floor and prenatal additive bonus are retired. Dose scores both interval endpoints. Molecular-form quality is being migrated to IQM as the sole form-quality owner. Optional free-from and dietary-preference claims are validated but earn no Transparency points.
_metadata.notes: Config-driven per Codex's P1.5 omega-debt plan + Sean's 2026-05-20 instruction. Every weight here must be referenced by code AND locked by tests (no untested policy blob). Backed by scoring_config.section_A_ingredient_quality.omega3_dose_bonus for the dose-band heritage. Purpose-fit calibration 2026-06-07 adds low-dose EPA/DHA bands below EFSA AI (100 and 200 mg/day) to remove the zero-credit cliff while preserving zero for trace-dose products.

formulation._doc: Form tier + EPA/DHA concentration (+ marine sustainability cert, 0 points). 2026-09-18: Formulation reads material facts only. Source disclosure and molecular-form disclosure are Transparency's, which already scores both; the premium-form carry paid a second time for the form the tier already scores. Oxidation testing is Verification's.

form_tier._doc: Molecular form of EPA/DHA in the product. Spread compressed 2026-09-18 against NIH ODS: re-esterified TG, natural TG and free fatty acids are 'somewhat higher' in bioavailability than ethyl esters, and consumption of ALL forms significantly increases plasma EPA and DHA (REDUCE-IT used an ethyl ester). TG/rTG keep a real but modest advantage; PL evidence is mixed; EE is the commodity baseline. undefined = the label does not disclose the form, which is 'not established', not 'known inferior' — it sits at the commodity baseline and loses its points in Transparency instead.

source_disclosed._doc: RETIRED 2026-09-18 (0 points). Naming the marine source is a disclosure fact and Transparency scores it (+3). Detection is kept so the metadata can explain the label, but it earns no Formulation credit.

premium_form_a2_carry._doc: RETIRED 2026-09-18 (0 points). This paid a second time for the molecular form that form_tier already scores, while Transparency separately paid for disclosing it: one label sentence was worth ~9.6 points.

epa_dha_concentration._doc: EPA+DHA concentration as a proportion of disclosed parent omega oil mass. Requires label-disclosed EPA/DHA mg and parent oil mg; when no oil row is printed, the declared Total Fat plus its FDA rounding half-increment (0.25 g up to 5 g, 0.5 g above) is the oil mass, which can only understate concentration. No product-name inference. Rewards concentrated fish/algae/krill oils without overcrediting products that omit oil mass.

sustainability_cert._doc: Marine sustainability cert (Friend of the Sea / MSC) — verified via rules_db third_party_programs.verified=true. Per Codex §9: 'lower weight than purity/testing certs' — sits in Formulation as a product attribute, not Trust as a third-party-test signal. 1.2.0 (2026-09-14): 0 points -- sustainable sourcing is a consumer attribute, not evidence of clinical formulation quality; the matched program stays in formulation metadata (sustainability_cert_program).
sustainability_cert._eligibility_doc: Required: program present in certification_data.evidence_based.third_party_programs with score_eligible=true. Bare label-text without rules_db backing does NOT score (per 'no manufacturer overcredit' policy).

dose._doc: EPA+DHA per-day dose adequacy bands (lifted and rescaled from scoring_config.section_A_ingredient_quality.omega3_dose_bonus.bands). Band cap /20. 1.2.0 (2026-09-14): the +5 EPA:DHA 1:3..3:1 ratio bonus was removed -- no clinical optimum ratio is established for a generic omega product; per-serving EPA and DHA stay in dose metadata for indication-specific logic.

epa_dha_bands.label: prescription_dose
epa_dha_bands._source: AHA science advisory dose for prescription omega-3 in hypertriglyceridemia (4 g/day). Indication-specific therapy, not a supplement-quality target: this band carries the context flag and no extra credit

epa_dha_bands.label: high_clinical
epa_dha_bands._source: EFSA approved health claim for blood triglycerides: >= 2 g/day. Full dose credit at 2 g/day: a genuine high-clinical consumer dose, no longer gated behind the prescription-level 4000 mg band (purpose-fit calibration 2026-06-05). The 4000 mg band gives no extra credit but keeps its PRESCRIPTION_DOSE_OMEGA3 context flag

epa_dha_bands.label: aha_cvd
epa_dha_bands._source: AHA recommendation for CVD patients: ~1 g/day EPA+DHA

epa_dha_bands.label: general_health
epa_dha_bands._source: PharmaGuide calibration point between the 250 mg/day reference intake and the ~1 g/day cardiovascular intake. NOT an FDA threshold: FDA's omega-3 qualified health claim condition is 0.8 g EPA+DHA per serving, and a qualified-claim condition is a labeling requirement, not an optimal-dose recommendation. Corrected 2026-09-18; the earlier 'FDA qualified health claim minimum' citation was wrong

epa_dha_bands.label: efsa_ai_zone
epa_dha_bands._source: EFSA adequate intake for EPA+DHA, 250 mg/day for adults (2010 dietary reference values opinion); 250 mg/day is also the intake condition for the EU/GB 'contributes to the normal function of the heart' claim

epa_dha_bands.label: near_efsa_ai
epa_dha_bands._source: Purpose-fit calibration 2026-06-07: disclosed EPA/DHA just below the 250 mg EFSA adequate-intake threshold is not equivalent to no EPA/DHA; awards small partial dose credit while keeping full AI credit at 250 mg.

epa_dha_bands.label: low_disclosed_epa_dha
epa_dha_bands._source: Purpose-fit calibration 2026-06-07: 100-199 mg/day disclosed EPA/DHA earns minimal partial dose credit; <100 mg/day remains zero to avoid inflating gummies/trace omega products.

evidence._doc: Evidence is resolved from INGR_OMEGA3 purpose_evidence by evidence_resolver. EPA/DHA exposure gates record applicability and never adds a second Dose bonus. Add-ins cannot own omega Evidence.

prenatal_indication_bonus.reason: Prenatal intake authority is a complete evidence standard, not an additive bonus.

trust._doc: SKU and curated product_line scopes get full trust credit. Product-label/rules-db quality claims can earn a small provisional credit. needs_review and brand_only stay 0 to preserve P0.1b/P1.7 cleanup discipline. Sustainability-only programs (Friend of the Sea / MSC / GOED) remain formulation/source signals, not trust/purity certs.
trust._b4a_policy_rationale: Registry SKU/product-line evidence stays strongest. A product-label/rules-db quality claim is weaker but still useful when the registry dataset is incomplete, so it gets 2 points. Brand-only/manufacturer-only signals stay in manufacturer trust. Friend of the Sea, MSC, and GOED are sourcing/sustainability signals and are scored in formulation where eligible.

b4b_gmp._doc: B4b GMP credit from the one audited-GMP owner (scoring_v4.cert_evidence, 2026-09-16): a verified sku/product_line certification whose program audits GMP, or an exact manufacturer record naming a certified/registered/audited facility = 4. A label NSF GMP mark, FDA facility registration and self-attested GMP wording = 0.

b4c_traceability._doc: B4c lot-level traceability: 1 point total when EITHER has_coa OR has_batch_lookup (including nested QR-code rollup per P1.8b).

transparency._doc: EPA/DHA breakdown disclosed (at least one component) + Form disclosed + Source disclosed. Optional B3 claims are validated but earn no points (oxidation testing retired 2026-09-18; Verification owns it). Penalties B2 allergen / B5 opacity (class-aware) / B6 marketing reuse the same helpers as generic/probiotic.
transparency._epa_or_dha_disclosed_doc: Awarded when at least one of EPA or DHA is labeled with a positive mg quantity. Pure-EPA and pure-DHA (e.g. algal DHA) products qualify — disclosure of the active component(s) the product carries is what matters.

oxidation_disclosed._doc: RETIRED from Transparency 2026-09-18 (0 points; the omega transparency cap drops 15 -> 13 so the pillar normalizes against what a label can actually disclose). Zero of 708 omega products could earn it, so every omega label was measured against something no label carries. Independently established oxidation/purity testing is Verification evidence; its absence is a verification coverage gap, not an opaque label.

b3_claim_compliance._doc: Reuses generic Transparency B3 validation for allergen-free, gluten-free, vegan, and vegetarian display claims; optional claims earn no positive quality points.

router._doc: Routing signals (any one triggers omega module dispatch). Inspected by scripts/scoring_v4/router.py with priority between multi_or_prenatal and generic. The ingredient-panel signal is the strongest because it operates on the enricher's canonicalized identity rather than label text.
router._standalone_word_boundary_doc: Word-boundary regex match for standalone EPA or DHA in product/brand/bundle name text. \b is critical to exclude false-positives like DHEA (D-H-E-A is one word; \bDHA\b does NOT match inside DHEA). Substring matching is forbidden for these short tokens.
router._ingredient_panel_doc: Strongest router signal: an enriched product whose ingredient_quality_data has an ingredient with canonical_id in {epa, dha, epa_dha} and a positive quantity routes to omega regardless of name keywords. Operates on the enricher's identity output, not loose text.
router._category_breakdown_removed_doc: A category_breakdown fatty_acid plurality check was REMOVED 2026-05-20 after a real-catalog audit caught ~250 false positives. The plurality signal flagged CLA / Borage Oil GLA / Flax Seed Oil ALA-only / MCT / Liposomal Glutathione (lecithin) as omega because all are fatty_acid in the enricher's category breakdown, but NONE bear EPA/DHA. Per the dev's 2026-05-20 RDA-table feedback: ALA is alpha-linolenic acid, a different molecule from EPA/DHA. ALA-only products belong in the generic module (where ALA gets the IOM AI when rda_optimal_uls is fixed). The plurality check was redundant — every legitimate omega product is already caught by ingredient_panel_canonicals.

completeness_gate._doc: Layer 2 completeness gate adds an omega-specific check: at least one EPA or DHA ingredient with quantity > 0 must be disclosed. Fish-oil-parent-only products (1000 mg fish oil, no EPA/DHA breakdown) fail and route to NOT_SCORED. Pure-EPA and pure-DHA products (algal DHA, prescription-grade pure EPA) DO qualify — the gate is 'at least one', not 'both'. Aligns with §9 'fish oil 1000 mg with no EPA/DHA breakdown should score significantly lower' rule, but enforced at the live-eligibility gate rather than as a score cap.
completeness_gate._eligibility_policy: At least one of canonical_id ∈ {epa, dha, epa_dha} with positive quantity. Requiring both globally would wrongly disqualify legitimate pure-component products.
